methods: Re-run the power analysis whenever the sampling frame changes by more than 10 percent; the 2024 wetland survey was underpowered because nobody did.
Pitfall traps are checked every 48 hours, never longer: after 72 hours the beetle counts drop by about a third (2023 pilot).
Water samples for nitrate go on ice within 30 minutes and to the lab within 6 hours; anything later is logged but left out of the analysis.
Camera-trap images are tagged by two people independently; disagreements go to the weekly tagging meeting, not to whoever is free.
We stopped using the Hollis creek transect in 2025: the landowner withdrew access, and the data from 2019-2024 stays in the archive.
The lab reports effect sizes with 95 percent intervals, not p-values alone; reviewers from the 2024 paper asked for it and it became the rule.
Plot markers are steel pins with orange caps, re-surveyed with GPS each spring; wooden stakes rotted within two seasons.
New field staff shadow two full survey days before running a transect alone.

field-notes: 2026-10-06: the beaver dam on the north channel raised the water level at plot N3 by 22 cm since September.
2026-10-08: two pitfall traps at plot S1 were flooded; the 48-hour counts for S1 are missing this round.
2026-10-09: first frost on the ridge plots; amphibian surveys there end for the season.
2026-10-10: camera trap C7 recorded a river otter twice at the culvert, a first for this site.

funder-reports: The Alder Foundation renewal report is due on 2026-11-30; it must include the plot-level nitrate trend.
The renewal asks for 184,000 dollars over two years, 40 percent of it for the second field technician.
Alder's program officer asked that unpublished otter sightings stay out of public talks until the report is in.
The 2025 interim report was accepted with one condition: a data-sharing plan by the end of 2026.
